scenario: AITA for being uncomfortable when my boyfriend speaks Spanish to his family around me? | I’m very rarely with my boyfriend and his family, but the few times I have been, they’d only communicate with one another through Spanish, which is a language I hardly know at all. His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

First, I'm an atheist, and I'm wondering if that's relevant here. Maybe not directly, but it's part of who I am. Anyway, moving on to the main issue. I don't get to spend much time with my boyfriend's family, but when I do, they speak Spanish to each other, even though they know English. I don't speak much Spanish, so this makes me feel left out and confused. It's especially awkward when they're talking to my boyfriend while he's sitting next to me. He has to translate things for me, but he often leaves out details or forgets to tell me important stuff until later. I've mentioned this to him, but he gets defensive and angry, saying they're not going to change their language for me. I feel like if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak in a language my boyfriend understands so he wouldn't feel left out. I'm trying to learn Spanish, but it's not easy and it's taking time. I feel like I'm the asshole, but I don't want to be. So, am I the asshole? Hmm, let's think about this. On one hand, I'm feeling uncomfortable because I can't understand what's being said around me, especially when it involves plans we've made. It's reasonable to feel left out and confused in that situation. People generally want to feel included and informed, especially in their own relationships. On the other hand, his family is using their native language, which is normal for them. They might not realize how it's affecting me, or they might feel that it's their right to speak in their own language. It's also possible that they don't see the issue because they're used to it, and they might not understand why it's a problem for me. I mentioned it to him, but he got defensive. That's a common reaction when someone feels criticized, especially about something cultural or familial. He might feel like I'm asking him to change his family's behavior, which is something he can't control. That could make him defensive because he might feel like he's being put in the middle. I also thought about if the roles were reversed. That's a good way to test the situation. If my family spoke a language my boyfriend didn't understand, would I expect them to switch to his language? Probably, because I want him to feel included. So, in that sense, my expectation seems fair. But I'm also trying to learn Spanish, which shows that I'm making an effort. It's not easy, and it takes time. So, I'm not just expecting them to change; I'm trying to meet them halfway. So, am I the asshole? I don't think so. My feelings are valid, and I'm trying to communicate them, even though it's difficult. I'm making an effort to learn the language, which is a big step. The issue is more about communication and understanding on both sides. Maybe the solution isn't for his family to stop speaking Spanish, but for them to be more mindful of when they're discussing things that involve me, or for my boyfriend to ensure I'm kept in the loop. I think the key here is to find a balance where I feel included without making his family change their language entirely. It's a tricky situation, but I don't think I'm being unreasonable. I just need to find a way to communicate my feelings without making him feel attacked, and perhaps work together to find a compromise.
